newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Saudi 97 wheat, barley support price same -analysts.
newsitem.headline: Saudi 97 wheat, barley support price same -analysts.

text.p: The price Saudi Arabia will pay most local grain farmers for their 1997 crops is unchanged at last year's levels of 1,500 riyals ($400) a tonne of wheat and 1,000 riyals a tonne of barley, farm analysts said.
"The support price is...1,500 riyals per tonne of wheat for small and medium-sized firms...1,200 riyals per tonne for larger firms," a Riyadh-based farm analyst told Reuters.
"Barley's support price is 1,000 riyals per tonne, the same as last year. There is no difference between big and small producers," he said.
The figures were confirmed by other agriculture experts in the kingdom, who said harvesting of this year's crop had begun.
Saudi Arabia is the world's biggest barley importer and analysts forecast imports of some six million tonnes this year.
Saudi-based analysts expect a 1997 wheat crop of 1.3-1.8 million tonnes, up from an estimated 1.0-1.2 million tonnes in 1996. Local consumption is about 1.8 million tonnes.
Grain experts say they expect barley production to hover around last year's estimated levels of 450,000 tonnes.
The support price for wheat has gone down sharply since it was introduced 15 years ago, experts said.

"The government has offered wheat incentives since 1982. The support price was 3,500 riyals per tonne from 1982 till about 1986. Then it came down to 2,000 riyals per tonne from 1986 to 1993. The it came down to 1,500 and 1,200 for big producers," one said.
